page.layout: One page of running text. Above the text, the running head. Beside line 12 in the right margin, one marginal note ("Cap.7."). The underlining in brown ink is a manuscript annotation and is not printed.

main_text.p: tum,quos statim excitat. Quod proculdubio haudquaquam præstaret, nisi spiritui, qui cum minuitur, præsentaneum esset fomentum,alimentumq;: At vinum, sicuti & quatuor nostri corporis humores, ex quatuor primis naturæ elementis constare nullimedico philosopho dubiũ est. Unde spiritum ab ijsdem elementis suam primam ducere originem,clarissimè patet: quādoquidem unũquodq; ex ijs alitur, è quibus oritur.Posthac an uno spiritu duntaxat sit præditū animal,scire licet. Fernelius enim Cap.7. libro de Spiritu,& innato calido,præter cæteros omnes medicos clariores diuidit spiritus in quosdam innatos,quos stabiles, & in unaquaque parte fixos esse ait, & in tres alios errantes & vagos, qui per universum corpus influit:unum videlicet naturalem è iecore per venas in corporis extrema diffusum:alterum vitalem, quem corasiduò [?] per arterias in universum corpus emittit: tertium animalem,qui in cerebri ventriculis genitus,hincque per neruos profectus, partes irrigat sensus motusque compotes. In primis,quòd ad insitum spiritu attinet, ipsum nō agnouerunt veteres medici, nec certè ullum esse rationi consentaneum videtur.

page.notes: Handwritten brown underlining over "an uno spiritu duntaxat sit præditū animal" and "libro de Spiritu" is manuscript, not print. Faint marks in the right margin are show-through or annotation and are left out. "corasiduò" is uncertain: the printed word may be "cor assiduò" in two words, so it is marked [?]. "quādo" is read from an acute-like mark over the a. The printed "dubiũ" and "unũquodq;" keep their tildes as printed.
